package_info.why_malicious: Versions 5.6.0 and 5.6.1 of xz Utils were intentionally backdoored to allow remote code execution (RCE) via SSH by subverting the liblzma library, which is used by OpenSSH. The malicious code was inserted by a trusted maintainer, enabling unauthorized access to affected systems.

execution_context.file_location: m4 macro script in xz tarball

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: m4 macro script that, during build, unpacks and executes additional bash scripts to deploy a malicious liblzma.o object file.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During build/install-time, the macro script unpacks and executes bash scripts that extract and deploy a malicious liblzma.o file, which is later linked into the system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Build scripts should not deploy or generate hidden binaries or object files outside of the expected build process.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal build macros only configure and prepare the build environment, not deploy hidden payloads.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Complex build systems may use macros for conditional compilation, but not for deploying hidden binaries.
key_indicators: Unpacking and executing hidden scripts during build

execution_context.file_location: bash scripts invoked by m4 macro

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Bash scripts that extract a malicious liblzma.o from the tarball and place it in the build output.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During build/install-time, the bash scripts extract a precompiled malicious object file (liblzma.o) and ensure it is linked into the final library.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Extracting and deploying precompiled object files is not standard for open-source builds, which should compile from source.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Open-source builds are expected to be reproducible from source, not to include hidden binaries.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious code in liblzma.o that hooks into the SSH authentication process, redirecting RSA_public_decrypt to backdoor logic.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when SSHD loads liblzma, the malicious code hooks into the authentication process, intercepts RSA_public_decrypt, and enables remote code execution via a crafted SSH key exchange.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: liblzma should not interact with SSH authentication or cryptographic routines.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Compression libraries are not expected to hook or modify authentication logic in SSHD.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; this is a clear violation of library boundaries.

attack_chain.action: Threat actor gains maintainer access and introduces malicious code into xz source tarballs.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is present in official xz releases.

attack_chain.action: During build/install, m4 macro and bash scripts deploy a malicious liblzma.o object file.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious object file is linked into the system's liblzma library.

attack_chain.action: When SSHD loads liblzma, the malicious code hooks into the authentication process.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker can trigger remote code execution via SSH.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses crafted SSH authentication to gain unauthorized access (RCE) on the victim system.

behavioral_signatures: Build scripts that unpack and execute hidden scripts or binaries
Presence of unexpected object files (liblzma.o) not matching source code
liblzma library code interacting with SSHD authentication routines
Redirection of cryptographic function pointers (e.g., RSA_public_decrypt) in SSHD
file_indicators: liblzma.o object file with unexpected or obfuscated content
xz tarballs containing hidden scripts or precompiled binaries
Unusual modifications in m4 macro scripts or build scripts
network_indicators: Unusual SSH authentication attempts with crafted keys
Unexpected SSHD process behavior or CPU usage
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor build processes for extraction or execution of hidden scripts or binaries. Analyze liblzma and related object files for code that interacts with SSHD or cryptographic routines. Check for redirection of function pointers in SSHD. Monitor for unusual SSH authentication attempts and unexpected SSHD resource usage. Compare built binaries against known-good versions and perform reproducible builds from source.
